title: Sheaves of modules on a ringed space have enough injectives
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is abelian and has enough injectives: every $\mathcal O_X$-module admits a monomorphism into an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (lemma-sheaves-modules-space), statement for an arbitrary ringed space

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of open subsets of $X$ with inclusions and open coverings as coverings; it is small, and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on it [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is the category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for this site. By the first clause of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category, in particular abelian; by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives, i.e. every $\mathcal O_X$-module admits a monomorphism into an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Lemma 01DI; via Injectives Theorem 079H (Grothendieck abelian categories have enough injectives) and Sites-cohomology Section 07A5 (Mod(O) is Grothendieck abelian)
